findings.finding: HMR rose +57% in four sessions into the print, from a 0.93 close on 11-23 to 1.46 on 11-27, and +44.6% over 5 days. Tanker peers rose +3.5% (NAT) and +5.3% (FRO) over the same days. Volume was 574k shares on the 11-27 half session against a 211k 20-day average, on a 6.04m-share float. No company release, filing or news explains it (the last release was 11-11, the last EDGAR filing 2026-09-09). The market has bid a large part of any good print in advance, which raises the real bar well above the $0.04 / $22m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: the stock ran +29% on 2026-05-22 (1.16 to 1.50) before the 05-26 print, rose +4.7% on the print day, then fell -20.4% on 05-27. Q2 2026 came after no run-up and still fell -10.8% on a revenue beat. Bars: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HMR?range=1y&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is priced by definition. The question is what it leaves for the release. Had the run been a sector move, FRO and NAT would be up by a similar amount, and they are up 3.5-5%. Had it been news-driven, a release or 6-K would exist, and none does. A 6m-share float moved by roughly 1m shares over three sessions is retail-driven positioning that tends to unwind on a print that merely meets the bar.

findings.finding: MR product-tanker spot earnings roughly halved from Q2 to Q3 2026. Ardmore's MR spot TCE was $27,031/day in Q3 against $51,870 in Q2 (-48%), reported 2026-11-03, after HMR last spoke on 09-01. HMR runs an MR pool, so its MR pool fees for Q3 fall with that rate. The consensus of $21.5-22.4m against Q2's $29.0m already assumes about a 24% sequential revenue drop.
findings.link: Same vessel class and same spot market: Heidmar operates an MR product-tanker pool (its pools run from MR to VLCC per https://www.lloydslist.com/LL1152722/Heidmar-eyes-growth-after-merger-and-listing). HMR's fees are a share of pool gross earnings. HMR's MR share of revenue is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HMR does not disclose pool TCEs or segment fees, so no reaction to this line has been observed.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Consensus revenue sits about 24% below Q2, consistent with analysts modelling lower Q3 product rates. What is not visible is HMR's own mix. Net of the rest: VLCC rates rose Q2 to Q3 (DHT Q3 fleet TCE $141.3k, profit $270.9m against $198.3m in Q2), and the fleet grew by 7 vessels in Q2, 3 takeovers expected in Q3 and Q-Shipping's 9 technical-management vessels from July 1. That is why this is small.
findings.independence: The CEO said on 2026-09-15 that product tankers had seen a 'massive decline in volume right now' (https://hellenicshippingnews.com/heidmar-ceo-sees-product-tanker-freight-lag-refining-margins). That is filed separately as a mid-quarter statement.

findings.finding: HMR's Q4 outlook commentary will describe October 2026, when crude tanker rates hit records. Ardmore's Q4 MR is booked at $57,600/day, against Q3's $27,031. HMR's pool fees scale with these rates, so a bullish Q4 statement is likely. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 09-01 management said rates would stay elevated into Q4/Q1, and the stock still fell -10.8%. Qualitative outlook has not bought this stock on the print day.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer bookings are public, and tanker equities have since fallen 16-20% from 10-30 on the November correction, so the sector has discounted the peak. What is not public is HMR's own Q4 pool earnings or fee run-rate. A first quantified Q4 figure from HMR would be new. If it were priced, HMR would have held up with the October rate peak, but it fell 51% from 10-13 to 11-23.

baseline_tension: There is no skew (no options market). The 5-day run-up of +44.6% against a flat-to-up sector cuts against a long on the print, and the evidence agrees with it: past prints have been sold, including a revenue beat. The 20-day -18% matches the tanker sector rather than signalling priced disappointment, and a bullish Q4 commentary is the main upside risk.
